tagline: The dragon-jar town on the Mae Klong River, home to Damnoen Saduak floating market, Khao Ngu caves, and the Tenasserim hills out at Suan Phueng
introHtml:
Ratchaburi sits west of Bangkok, about a two-hour drive away. People know it for the glazed dragon jars potters have made here for generations, which earned it the nickname the jar town. The city center sits on the Mae Klong River, with old markets and riverside temples to wander.

The western side of the province is Suan Phueng and Ban Kha districts, up against the Tenasserim Range along the Myanmar border. It's cooler than the city, with resorts, grasslands, and waterfalls. The Damnoen Saduak side is flat orchard country, home to the Damnoen Saduak floating market where people come from early morning to watch vendors paddle boats and sell their goods.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable, good for heading up to Suan Phueng and walking the floating market. In the rainy season the waterfalls along the Tenasserim hills run full and the landscape turns lush green

highlights.name: Ratchaburi dragon jars
highlights.blurb: Old kilns have been turning out glazed earthenware jars with dragon motifs for decades, until they became the town's signature. Stop by the roadside potteries to watch the throwing and buy a piece to take home

highlights.name: Damnoen Saduak floating market
highlights.blurb: An old floating market where vendors paddle boats along the canals selling food and fruit. It's busy from early morning and it's the canal scene people picture when they think of Ratchaburi

highlights.name: Suan Phueng
highlights.blurb: A district up in the Tenasserim Range along the border, cool air, with resorts, grasslands, streams, and a sheep farm. People like to stay overnight up here to escape the heat in town

highlights.name: Khao Ngu caves and Khao Kaen Chan
highlights.blurb: Limestone hills near the city with caves holding old Buddha images and a viewpoint up top. Khao Kaen Chan has a large Buddha image and a view looking down over Ratchaburi town

highlights.name: The old town on the Mae Klong River
highlights.blurb: The old market quarter and shophouses along the Mae Klong River in the city, with old temples, coffee shops, and the Ratchaburi National Museum in the former provincial hall building

highlights.name: Khu Bua teen jok weaving and the Thai Song Dam people
highlights.blurb: Ban Khu Bua is a center for weaving teen jok cloth in old patterns by the Thai Yuan people, while several districts have Thai Song Dam communities that still keep their own culture and food

foodScene.name: Eats at Damnoen Saduak floating market
foodScene.note: In the morning there's boat noodles, khanom khrok, old-style coffee, and orchard fruit sold from boats. You can graze along the canal as you go

foodScene.name: Boat noodles
foodScene.note: Stalls around the Damnoen Saduak canals have long served rich nam tok boat noodles. The bowls are small so you order several, a classic pairing with the floating market

foodScene.name: Thai Song Dam food
foodScene.note: The Thai Song Dam communities in the province have their own local dishes, such as sour bamboo-shoot curry, Thai Song Dam khao lam, and bold dipping-sauce plates

foodScene.name: Damnoen orchard fruit
foodScene.note: The Damnoen Saduak plain grows grapes, rose apples, aromatic coconut, and guava, in season for buying fresh from the orchards along the canals

foodScene.name: Sweets and coconut sugar
foodScene.note: Coconut groves around Damnoen make fresh coconut sugar that goes into desserts, from thong yot to khanom mo kaeng and sticky rice with coconut

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and along the Mae Klong River
foodScene.note: The old town has cafes set in shophouses and riverside coffee shops, some in old jar kilns, an easy place to sip coffee and take in the town

foodScene.name: Streamside restaurants at Suan Phueng
foodScene.note: The Suan Phueng side has restaurants and cafes along the streams in cool surroundings, where you can order grilled fish and som tam under the trees

foodScene.name: Souvenirs from the jar town
foodScene.note: Besides pottery, there are souvenirs like kun chiang sausage, processed fruit, and Khu Bua woven cloth to take home

attractions.name: Damnoen Saduak floating market
attractions.blurb: An old canalside floating market where vendors paddle boats selling food and fruit, busy from early morning

attractions.name: Dragon jar kilns
attractions.blurb: Kilns that make the glazed earthenware dragon jars the town is known for. Stop by to watch the throwing and buy a piece to take home

attractions.name: Suan Phueng
attractions.blurb: A district up in the Tenasserim Range along the border, cool air, with grasslands, streams, and a sheep farm to visit

attractions.name: Khao Ngu caves
attractions.blurb: Limestone hills near the city with caves enshrining old Buddha images carved into the walls. You can walk up to see the caves and the town view

attractions.name: Khao Kaen Chan
attractions.blurb: A low hill in the city with a large Buddha image up top and a viewpoint looking down over Ratchaburi town

attractions.name: Ratchaburi National Museum
attractions.blurb: A museum in the old provincial hall building by the Mae Klong River, displaying antiquities from the city of Khu Bua and the town's history

attractions.name: Ban Khu Bua and teen jok weaving
attractions.blurb: A Thai Yuan community that weaves teen jok cloth in old patterns, with a weaving center and the ancient Khu Bua city ruins to see

attractions.name: Kao Chon waterfall and Bo Khlueng hot springs
attractions.blurb: Waterfalls and hot springs along the Tenasserim Range on the Suan Phueng–Ban Kha side, at their best in the rainy season when the water is high
